issue.title: Decide and enforce the access boundary for rfserver's token-authed function port 23401 on athena

task_type_fields.impact: A mail-sending endpoint protected only by a static token is reachable from LAN and tailnet, and possibly the public internet through DDNS. A leaked token or a token-check weakness turns athena into a mail relay.
task_type_fields.repro:
On athena, 2026-10-23:

```bash
ss -ltn | grep ':23401'                                    # 0.0.0.0:23401 LISTEN
ssh apollo 'timeout 4 bash -c "</dev/tcp/100.87.31.114/23401" && echo open'   # open
```

rfserver (Bryan's user Supervisor program `tools:rfserver`, source `~/db/bin/main/rfuncs/server.py`) serves its function port 23401 on every interface, including a token-authenticated `/sendmail` endpoint. `RFSERVER_HOSTNAME=bbugyi.ddns.net` (public DDNS) suggests clients reach it by that public name, so a blind loopback rebind could break local pymail callers or other clients. Phase bob-cli-an.3 rebound only rfserver's `/metrics` listener (9101) to loopback and left 23401 alone on purpose. Its nftables table `inet athena_monitoring` covers only ports 9090/9091/9100/9101/9102.

Needed: inventory 23401 clients (local pymail, other hosts, anything resolving bbugyi.ddns.net) and check router port-forwarding and public reachability. Then choose loopback, tailnet-only plus firewall, or an authenticated proxy, apply it through a reviewed sudo gate if firewall changes are needed, and verify both allowed and denied probes. Proposed by bob-cli-an.3 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #3). Size large because the client set and public exposure are unknown.

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-an.3 restricted the monitoring listeners but intentionally left rfserver's 0.0.0.0:23401 /sendmail port because its clients (possibly via public DDNS) were not inventoried.

payload.description: Both are remaining 0.0.0.0 control listeners on athena found while landing bob-cli-an; firewall work could be coordinated
